title: Shared HIP scheduler and work-queue strategy
description:
Define and validate a reusable CPU/GPU scheduling strategy for HIP kernels.

## Background

The existing BCJR HIP path uses default-stream launches and full-device synchronization. That can serialize or contend when many CPU threads submit GPU work. This story measures that risk and establishes a shared scheduler model for BCJR, LDPC BP, BCH syndrome evaluation, and future HIP kernels.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Direct per-thread/default-stream submission is measured against a shared GPU-owner scheduler on the existing BCJR path.
- [hard] The scheduler prototype covers bounded queueing, batch coalescing, stream/event completion, and backpressure policy.
- [hard] The comparison is extended to LDPC BP or BCH syndrome once one candidate microkernel exists.
- [hard] Measurements include CPU thread count, batch size, stream count, and phase breakdown where practical.
- [hard] The final recommendation specifies the reusable ownership model, queue policy, batching granularity, stream usage, completion signaling, and CPU work partitioning.

## Notes

Spec doc: `dev/plans/hip_gpu_prototype_wave.md`. This story depends on GPU evidence infrastructure.
